question: What is the nominal voltage of the DA40 electrical system?
explanation: The DA40 uses a 28 volt DC system fed by an engine-driven alternator, with a 24 volt battery as the standby source. Any replacement battery, ground power unit or portable equipment must match this 28 volt architecture - connecting a 12 volt ground power unit is not acceptable.
reference: Airplane Flight Manual, Section 7 - Electrical System

question: In flight the ALTERNATOR warning illuminates and the ammeter shows a discharge. What is the immediate consequence for the pilot?

options.text: The engine will stop within a few minutes because ignition depends on the alternator
All electrical services are lost instantly
Electrical services now run from the battery only, for a limited time
Nothing changes, because the battery charges the system in flight

explanation: With the alternator offline the battery becomes the only source of electrical power, so endurance is limited and non-essential loads should be shed and a landing planned. The engine itself keeps running: ignition is provided by engine-driven magnetos, which are independent of the aircraft electrical system.
reference: Airplane Flight Manual, Section 3 - Emergency Procedures
